notes.summary: Conditional noninvariant Gauss domination and convexity: scalar-extended annular comparison bounds every finite continuous scalar-curve-positive torus function by a convex Gauss-point restriction. Generic scalar coefficients are essential. No exact real-PL or classification conclusion is claimed.
notes.detailedSummary: Assuming explicit annular comparison over every complete analytic extension, prove that a finite continuous scalar-curve-positive function h on an open convex tropical torus domain satisfies h(x) ≤ h(κ(τ(x))), and that t ↦ h(κ(t)) is convex. Domination uses successive independent Gauss variables and singleton-boundary comparison. Convexity uses a monomial curve over the completed residue field of a multidimensional Gauss point, preventing cancellation of grouped coefficients. The argument admits noninvariant functions and essential scalar extensions. Applicability of the comparison foundation to the unavailable exact primary classical definition remains unverified.
notes.text:
Assume foundation F1: scalar-curve-positive functions pull back to subharmonic functions on smooth strict open annuli over every complete analytic extension. On a closed strict annulus, harmonic comparison with \(A+B\log|u|\) uses its two Gauss endpoints; on \(|u|=1\), constant comparison uses the singleton Gauss boundary. This is an explicit assumption, not a result granted by the supplied book or audits. The exact primary definition was not retrieved.

Let \(K\) be complete and nontrivially valued, \(T=(\mathbf G_{m,K}^n)^{\mathrm{an}}\), \(\tau(x)=(\log|Z_i(x)|)_i\), \(\Omega\subset\mathbf R^n\) open convex, and \(U=\tau^{-1}(\Omega)\). Define \(\kappa_K(t)\) by
\[
\left|\sum_m c_mZ^m\right|_{\kappa_K(t)}=\max_m|c_m|e^{\langle m,t\rangle}.
\]
Weighted Gauss multiplicativity follows because initial forms multiply in a Laurent polynomial ring over the graded residue field, an integral domain. This defines a torus point with tropical coordinate \(t\). Its dependence on \(t\) is continuous in the Laurent-polynomial evaluation topology. Let \(h\) be finite continuous and scalar-curve-positive. No invariance is assumed.

Fix \(x\), set \(t=\tau(x)\), and take \(E=\mathcal H(x)\), with coordinate images \(a_i\in E^\times\), \(|a_i|=e^{t_i}\). The rational \(E\)-point \((a_i)\) projects to \(x\). Choose \(\epsilon>0\) such that \(t+se_j\in\Omega\) for all \(j\) and \(|s|<\epsilon\). If necessary, adjoin a weighted Gauss variable of norm \(e^\epsilon\) and complete its rational-function field, making surrounding annuli strict while preserving original norms.

Adjoin independent radius-one Gauss variables \(S_1,\ldots,S_j\), completing to fields \(E_j\). Let \(x_j\) be the projected point obtained by substituting \(Z_i=a_iS_i\) for \(i\le j\), and \(Z_i=a_i\) otherwise. Over \(E_{j-1}\), use the open-annulus curve
\[
u\longmapsto(a_1S_1,\ldots,a_{j-1}S_{j-1},a_ju,a_{j+1},\ldots,a_n).
\]
Its point \(u=1\) projects to \(x_{j-1}\), and its unit Gauss point projects to \(x_j\). F1 gives \(h(x_{j-1})\le h(x_j)\). Finally,
\[
\left|\sum_m c_ma^mS^m\right|=\max_m|c_m|e^{\langle m,t\rangle},
\]
so \(x_n=\kappa_K(t)\). Thus \(h(x)\le h(\kappa_K(\tau(x)))\).

For convexity, put \(a_h(t)=h(\kappa_K(t))\). Fix an integer direction \(w\) and a compact segment \(t_0+rw\subset\Omega\). Take \(E=\mathcal H(\kappa_K(t_0))\), with coordinate images \(a_i\), and consider \(\gamma(u)=(a_i u^{w_i})_i\). For \(P=\sum_m c_mZ^m\), its coefficient of \(u^k\) after substitution is
\[
B_k=\sum_{\langle m,w\rangle=k}c_ma^m.
\]
The defining Gauss norm gives
\[
|B_k|=\max_{\langle m,w\rangle=k}|c_m|e^{\langle m,t_0\rangle}.
\]
Consequently the radius-\(e^r\) Gauss point of this curve projects exactly to \(\kappa_K(t_0+rw)\). Desired endpoint and exterior radii can be realized in another complete weighted-Gauss field extension, making the closed and surrounding open annuli strict without changing these coefficient norms. F1 compared with the harmonic endpoint chord proves
\[
a_h(t_0+((1-\theta)r_0+\theta r_1)w)
\le(1-\theta)a_h(t_0+r_0w)+\theta a_h(t_0+r_1w).
\]
Every rational direction is proportional to an integer direction. Approximating arbitrary displacements by rational vectors and using continuity proves full convexity.

The scalar coefficients are essential. The ground-field diagonal \(u\mapsto(u,u)\) annihilates \(Z_1-Z_2\), whereas its norm at the two-dimensional unit Gauss point is \(1\), in every residue characteristic. Thus an ordinary ground-field monomial curve does not realize the required multidimensional Gauss section. The completed-residue-field calculation repairs that cancellation. This is an algebraic observation, not an envelope counterexample.

This is a proved mathematical implication under F1, not an exhaustive finite result or experiment. Identification of F1 with the intended classical definition remains unverified; membership of the exact LFS and real-PL classes is not established here. The complete argument is in P03.1-argument.md and P03.1-paper.tex. Regenerate the TeX source with python3 make-paper.py and compile twice with python3 rerun.py. No supplied or earlier local result is used.

notes.summary: Conditional full-family toric computation and scalar compatibility: bounded open convex tropical domains and tropical usc obstacles with a finite convex minorant have full noninvariant scalar-psh and conventional LFS envelopes equal to the convex tropical envelope. The exact P03 union still requires an unproved real-PL bridge; the sharp classification remains unsolved.
notes.detailedSummary: Using n1 and explicit unit-harmonic and LFS-presentation foundations, compute the entire continuous scalar-curve-positive and entire locally LFS minorant envelopes, including noninvariant competitors. Gauss restriction supplies the upper bound for every competitor. Supporting planes and rational-slope approximation with a bounded-domain downward correction supply global LFS minorants achieving the lower bound. Applying the computation over every analytic extension proves compatibility of the separately defined full families and commutation of regularization with scalar pullback in this sector. The original union conclusion is conditional on scalar-stable positivity of every exact semipositive real-PL competitor. Foundational verification, arbitrary obstacles, target relative boundary, sharp normal/unibranch hypotheses and branch/pinching necessity remain unresolved.
notes.text:
Retain n1 and assume \(\Omega\) is bounded. Add two explicit foundations. F2: on every test curve required by the intended classical definition, over every complete analytic extension, logarithms of analytic units are harmonic; real linear combinations remain harmonic; harmonic comparison defines a local subharmonicity calculus. Singular test curves are included if required by that definition. F3: the LFS class has conventional local presentations
\[
h=m^{-1}\max_i(\lambda_i+\log|g_i|),\qquad m\in\mathbf Z_{>0},\quad\lambda_i\in\mathbf R,
\]
with analytic generators having no common zero, including rational-slope monomials and common-denominator finite maxima. These foundations and their identification with the original classes were not verified from a retrieved primary proof.

Let \(\varphi:\Omega\to\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\) be usc with a finite convex minorant \(a_0\), let \(f=\varphi\circ\tau\), and set
\[
p=\sup\{a:\Omega\to\mathbf R\text{ finite convex},\ a\le\varphi\}.
\]
The minorant excludes \(-\infty\) values of \(\varphi\); its codomain excludes \(+\infty\). Hence \(a_0\le p\le\varphi\) is finite, and taking suprema of convex inequalities proves convexity. On a compact ball inside \(\Omega\), usc bounds \(\varphi\) above and continuity of finite convex \(a_0\) bounds it below. Extending convex chords from points in the quarter-radius ball at least half the original radius bounds both secant slopes by \(2(M-m)/R\), proving local Lipschitz continuity of \(p\). Continuity of finite convex \(a_0\) follows by the same argument, with upper bounds supplied by surrounding box vertices and lower bounds by reflection about its center. No common modulus for the analytic competitor family is assumed.

Let \(\mathcal C_{K,f}\) be the entire finite continuous scalar-curve-positive minorant family. For each of its members, n1 makes \(a_h(t)=h(\kappa_K(t))\) a convex minorant of \(\varphi\), and proves
\[
h(x)\le a_h(\tau(x))\le p(\tau(x)).
\]
This covers all noninvariant members.

To prove positivity and the reverse inequality, finite convex \(p\) has global supporting affine functions at every interior point. Indeed, local Lipschitz bounds make its directional derivative finite and sublinear; finite-dimensional sublinear extension supplies a dominated linear functional, and convexity turns it into a global support. Supports represent \(p\). On any compact subset, continuity of their gaps and a finite cover give uniform approximation from below by finite maxima of supports.

After every complete analytic extension \(E/K\) and every required curve map \(g:C\to U_E\), the coordinate pullbacks \(G_i=Z_i\circ g\) are units. F2 makes each affine tropical support pull back to a harmonic real linear combination of \(\log|G_i|\). Finite maxima of harmonic functions are subharmonic by boundary comparison of each summand. Locally uniform limits preserve comparison: uniform boundary error \(\epsilon\) permits comparison against the harmonic comparator plus \(\epsilon\), followed by the limit and \(\epsilon\downarrow0\). Therefore \(p\circ\tau\) is finite continuous scalar-curve-positive and below \(f\). Thus the entire family \(\mathcal C_{K,f}\) has raw envelope \(p\circ\tau\).

Under F2-F3, every locally LFS function is scalar-curve-positive. Its presentation survives scalar extension and curve pullback. At a curve point some generator is nonzero. Terms vanishing there can be discarded on a small neighborhood because they lie below a finite nonzero term. Remaining generators become units on a smaller neighborhood, so the function is locally a positive multiple of a finite maximum of harmonic functions. Comparison and locality prove positivity on the entire test curve. Thus the upper bound applies to the full noninvariant LFS family \(\mathcal L_{K,f}\).

For its lower bound, fix \(t_0\) and a support \(\ell(t)=p(t_0)+\langle b,t-t_0\rangle\). Put \(D=\sup_{t\in\Omega}\|t-t_0\|<\infty\). For rational \(q\), define
\[
\ell_q(t)=p(t_0)+\langle q,t-t_0\rangle-D\|q-b\|.
\]
Cauchy-Schwarz gives \(\ell_q\le\ell\le p\le\varphi\) everywhere, while \(\ell_q(t_0)\to p(t_0)\). For \(q=v/m\), its pullback is \(c+m^{-1}\log|Z^v|\), a global LFS minorant by F3. Consequently
\[
\sup\mathcal L_{K,f}=p\circ\tau=\sup\mathcal C_{K,f}.
\]
Boundedness is used in the downward correction; no full LFS equality on an unbounded tropical domain is asserted. Compact exhaustion and finite covers give finite maxima approximating \(p\) locally uniformly. Cumulative maxima make them increasing, and common slope denominators provide LFS presentations. These supply a lower bound for the full family, whose upper bound already holds for every competitor.

The computation over every complete analytic extension has the identical \(\Omega,\varphi,p\). Since \(\tau_E=\tau_K\circ\pi_{E/K}\), the separately defined full families satisfy
\[
\sup\mathcal L_{E,f\circ\pi_{E/K}}
=(\sup\mathcal L_{K,f})\circ\pi_{E/K}=p\circ\tau_E,
\]
and likewise for \(\mathcal C\). The computed raw envelopes are continuous, so
\[
(s_K\circ\pi_{E/K})^*=s_K^*\circ\pi_{E/K}=p\circ\tau_E.
\]
This proves the conditional scalar compatibility without assuming scalar projection is open or mistaking ground-field curve tests for scalar stability.

For the original union \(\mathcal E\), the missing bridge is that every exact semipositive real-PL competitor is finite continuous scalar-curve-positive after every analytic extension. If established together with F1-F3, then \(\mathcal L\subseteq\mathcal E\subseteq\mathcal C\) squeezes the entire original union envelope to the same function over every field. This implication requires neither fiberwise-maximum closure nor a PL/LFS approximation theorem. The real-PL bridge is not proved here.

Even with that bridge, the result treats only tropical obstacles with a finite convex minorant on bounded convex smooth-torus domains. Arbitrary obstacles, minus-infinity cases outside this scope, target relative boundary, singular normal/unibranch targets, sharp sufficiency and necessity, and branched/nonsplit-node/codimension-two pinching obstructions remain unresolved. No CLD-v2 claim or solution of P03.3 is made. The literal original P03.1 target is not solved.

Complete proof and gates are recorded in P03.1-argument.md, P03.1-paper.tex, source-provenance.json, and status.json. Run python3 make-paper.py followed by python3 rerun.py. Mathematical support is n1; compilation is not mathematical support.
